papers.title: PURE: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multi-Granularity Multimodal Identity Matching
papers.problem: Online shops cannot tell if two listings show the same product, and one accuracy score hides why models fail.
papers.fix: The PURE test scored ten AI models from 47.1% to 86.0%, and evidence-based judgment scored lowest.
papers.practicalUseCase: A high matching score can hide weak spots, so test models on each skill before you trust them.
papers.limitation: The test uses online shopping data only, so results may differ in other fields.

papers.title: Time Series Structure Learning with Local Causal Parent Discovery
papers.problem: Finding cause and effect in time data runs slowly because tests grow costly as the number of variables grows.
papers.fix: The ITPD method ran 2.3, 9.1, and 40.9 times faster than three rival methods on 2000-variable graphs.
papers.practicalUseCase: If your data has thousands of variables, this method finds causes far faster, so try it before older tools.
papers.limitation: The speed results come from simulated data, not real-world data.

papers.title: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Stop Safely
papers.problem: Robots told to stop a banned task midway often still finish it or drop the object they hold.
papers.fix: The SAFI method cut banned-task success after takeover to 1.3%, with no recorded physical incidents.
papers.practicalUseCase: A robot can learn to freeze safely mid-task, so train a hold response instead of only refusing at the start.
papers.limitation: Tests covered one robot model on LIBERO tasks, and only tasks where holding still is a safe response.

papers.title: PAD: Policy-Aware Data Valuation for Autonomous Driving
papers.problem: More driving demonstration data does not always help, because one planner gains from data that another planner wastes.
papers.fix: The PAD method improved the driving score by 3.5 points on NavTest and 5.0 points on NavHard.
papers.practicalUseCase: Choose training data for each target model instead of piling up more data, which also reduces scene-level regressions.
papers.limitation: Results come from one driving score on benchmark tests, not real roads.

papers.title: Islamic Social Financial Instruments and Sustainable Community Development: Evidence Synthesis on Community Resilience
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Research on zakat, waqf, and sadaqah is scattered, so nobody knew how each one helps communities cope with hardship.
papers.fix: A review of 93 studies found zakat gives short-term relief, waqf builds long-term assets, and sadaqah gives flexible emergency help.
papers.practicalUseCase: Use zakat for crisis relief and waqf for lasting projects, and combine all three with strong governance.
papers.limitation: This review summarises past studies, so it shows patterns across papers but does not prove cause.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk grew fast, but nobody had mapped who issues them or what makes an issue bigger.
papers.fix: In 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, growth centres in Indonesia, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, and equity-based contracts give bigger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers who want bigger sukuk should pick equity-based contracts and watch second party opinion costs, which shrink issue size.
papers.limitation: The data ends in 2022, so it may miss newer market changes.

papers.title: From Clicks to Credit: AI-Measured Halal Product Awareness and Halal Financing Depth across OIC Countries
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks lacked proof that consumer interest in halal products leads to more Islamic financing.
papers.fix: In 16 OIC countries from 2014 to 2023, more halal searches raised Islamic financing, mostly through Murabaha and Ijarah.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks can read halal search trends as demand signals and offer simple Murabaha and Ijarah products first.
papers.limitation: Online search interest stands in for real awareness, and the effect on Mudarabah and Musharakah is weak.

papers.title: Islamic Banking Products Accessibility and SME Performance: Evaluating Shari’ah-Compliant Financial Solutions for Somali Enterprises
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.leadAuthor: Ali Yassin Sheikh Ali et al.
papers.problem: Small firms in Baidoa, Somalia, may not gain from Islamic banking, and nobody knew which barrier matters most.
papers.fix: Affordability and ease of access drove small business performance most, while awareness had little direct effect.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks should cut costs and simplify service first, because telling owners about products alone changes little.
papers.limitation: The survey covers one Somali city at one point in time, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Examining the Impact of Waqf Literacy on Waqf Behaviour
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Waqf collection stays low, and it was unclear whether knowing about waqf makes Muslims give.
papers.fix: Among 642 Indonesian Muslims, waqf literacy raised attitude, social norms, and control, which then lifted the intention to donate.
papers.practicalUseCase: Teach people how waqf works to raise giving, because knowledge changes intention through those three factors.
papers.limitation: The survey covers Indonesia only, and it measures intention to give rather than actual donations.
